methods.label: Divide one circumference by the speed
methods.explanation:
One trip around the equator covers the circumference of a circle. Because the flight height is negligible, we use the given radius of \(4000\) miles. The estimated distance is
\[
2\pi\cdot4000=8000\pi\text{ miles}.
\]
At \(500\) miles per hour, the time is distance divided by speed:
\[
\frac{8000\pi}{500}=16\pi\text{ hours}.
\]
Using \(\pi\approx3.14\) gives \(16\cdot3.14=50.24\) hours. This is much closer to \(50\) than to \(25\) or \(75\), and the other choices are farther away. The best estimate is \(\boxed{50\text{ hours}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
